$comment: Riftlight, Forgotten Paths middle (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, the-wrong-valley; design note memory-paths-continuity-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 to the pilot's bar. Question: where is this river going, and why? Hummock, the yeti route worker, carries it with Pip. The p2 (old_road) is the oldest marker's wavy line: the river runs an old course. Force (wall it off) or understand (watch it run). Thornguard holds the ice. Sets valley_crossed_high (how the party crossed, read by reading-room) and wrong_valley_witnessed on every path; reads stone_route_priority.
title: The River Takes Another Valley

plate.narration: Two valleys run between the glacier ridges. An old path follows one; fresh water fills the other. High on the slope, a chipped stone marker still points along the ridge.

goal.text: Where is this river going, and why?

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The river is not angry; it is going somewhere it used to go.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.route_worker_yeti: Hummock, the yeti route worker (he/him). Enormous, slow and kind; says "Steady on"; names every rock on his route and thaws his frozen eyebrows in his tea. Keeps the markers and the warning post on the valley road. Wants the evening sled warned and to know where his river has gone.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants to impress her. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.
npcVoices.Grandma Drift: Yeti grandmother who drives the evening sled from the singing hall (she/her). Brisk and warm; wears a scarf three times her length; remembers old stories.

arrival.narration: North of the counting stones, the road climbs toward the glacier. Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, unrolls his map. "Dry valley ahead." A river roars down it. Pip turns the map upside down. The river is still there. Below, an enormous yeti waves a lantern on a pole. "Stay up there! I'm Hummock. I keep the markers on this road. The river came down the wrong valley this morning. Where is it going? And why? Help me find out, and warn the evening sled before it drives into it!"

snowbank.narration: The bank is steep, snowy and very slidey. Hummock plants his pole at the bottom like a goalpost. "Feet first!"
snowbank.prompt: Slide down the snowbank without shooting into the river

onSuccess.narration: You whoosh down and stop neatly against Hummock's pole. Pip lands on his notebook.

onFailure.narration: You spin, bump and land headfirst in a drift. Hummock pulls you out by the boots, and it takes a while to find Pip's map. "Steady on."

meet_hummock.narration: Hummock's eyebrows have frozen into two icicles. He thaws them in his tea, one at a time. "My warning post is over there, on the far bank," he says. "Every evening a sled comes down from the singing hall, along this valley, because it's always been dry. Tonight it isn't." He pats a boulder. "That's Gertrude. I name all my rocks. They stay where I put them."

look.narration: Pip holds up his map. "Lady Olivia says a good map is never wrong. Only the land can be." Ridges, markers, the river, the dry valley. Something here has moved. How can you tell what?

choices.label: Hold Pip's map up to the valley
Climb Gertrude for a better look
Lay Tally's road plan over the valley

variants.text: Pip pats his notebook. "And we have Tally's road plan. Every landmark counted!"
Pip pats his rubbing of the old carved mountain. "No help here," he admits. "But it's very nice."

check_map.narration: The wind keeps folding the map in half. Pip holds one corner in his teeth. "Mmf," he says helpfully.
check_map.prompt: Match the map's ridges and markers to the valley

onSuccess.narration: Ridge, ridge, marker, marker. Everything matches.

onFailure.narration: You match the wrong ridge, and for a while you think the mountains moved. Hummock gently turns you around. That took a while.

check_climb.narration: Gertrude is tall, round and slippery. "She doesn't mind feet," says Hummock.

onSuccess.narration: From the top you can see the whole valley, every ridge and marker in its place.

onFailure.narration: You slide off twice. The third time, Hummock lifts you up like a kitten. It all takes ages.

check_plan.narration: Tally counted every landmark on her road plan, and numbered them. Some you can see from here.
check_plan.prompt: Find Tally's counted landmarks in the valley

onSuccess.narration: Tally's landmarks line up, one, two, three. Quick work. "She'd be proud," says Pip.

onFailure.narration: The plan's landmarks are far away and small. It takes a while to line them up, but they do.

read_valley.narration: The ridges are where they should be. Hummock's markers stand in their rows. Only the river has moved, right out of its own valley and into this dry one. "So the map's right," says Pip slowly, "and the river is the one being wrong." "Let's see where it turns," says Hummock.

bank_path.narration: Stepping stones run up the edge of the rushing water. They were dry this morning. Now each one wears a little hat of foam. "Hop lively," says Hummock.
bank_path.prompt: Hop the wet stepping stones up to where the river turns

onSuccess.narration: Hop, hop, hop. Dry boots. Hummock just walks, because his legs are as long as you are.

onFailure.narration: A stone wobbles, and you sit down in the shallows. Hummock fishes you out and wrings out your sleeves. That cost time.

fork.narration: At the top of the valley, the river splits. It always went left, down its own valley. Today it goes right. You look for what pushed it. No ice. No fallen rocks. No beaver with big plans. The river just turns, smooth as a ribbon, with nothing in its way. "Like it remembers the road," says Hummock.

old_road.narration: By the fork stands Hummock's oldest marker, a stone post older than anyone's grandmother. He rubs off the frost. Carved on it is a wavy line, pointing right, down the valley that was dry. "That never made sense," he whispers. "The river never went that way." High on the old valley's walls lie round river stones, dry for ages. This river is running down a road it ran long, long ago. Your Listening Chime swings north on its string, toward the glacier, and hums.

choices.label: Follow the water down the old valley

down_valley.narration: The water rushes on down the old valley, filling pools that have been empty forever. "Where's it going?" cries Pip, already running. How will you keep up?

choices.label: Ride a board down the snow beside it
Stamp a trail along the rim with Hummock

check_board.narration: Hummock lends you a flat board he uses for carrying signs. "It's not a sled," he warns. The board does not care.
check_board.prompt: Steer the board down the snowy slope beside the river

onSuccess.narration: Whoosh! You zip down beside the water and skid to a stop at the top of a cliff.

onFailure.narration: The board goes left. You go right, into a snowbank, and roll the rest of the way, very fast and very round. Digging out takes ages.

check_trail.narration: The snow is waist deep on you and knee deep on Hummock. "Lift your knees," he says, as if that helps.
check_trail.prompt: Stamp a trail through the deep snow along the rim

onSuccess.narration: You stamp a good trail. Pip follows in it, singing marching songs.

onFailure.narration: The snow wins for a while. By the time you reach the cliff, everyone is puffing and the sun is lower.

old_falls.narration: At the cliff, an old waterfall has woken up. Its stone lip is worn smooth from long ago, and the water pours over it as if it never stopped. Below, a dry lake bed is filling. Two ducks sit in the middle, very surprised. "It's going home," says Pip. "To an old home."

pip_dam.narration: Pip's eyes shine. "Lady Olivia says if the land goes wrong, you put it right! We could wall off the old valley at the fork and push the river home!" Hummock scratches his ear. "A wall is quick. But the water would pile up over the low ice where we cross, right by my oldest marker. Or we let it run and watch where it goes. That takes longer, and the sled comes at dusk." What will you do?

choices.label: Wall off the old valley at the fork

check_wall.narration: Back at the fork, everyone heaves rocks. Hummock carries three at once. Pip carries one, with great ceremony. "Faster!" he shouts.
check_wall.prompt: Pile rocks across the fork fast enough to turn the river

onSuccess.narration: The wall holds. The river slews left, back toward its own valley. Pip cheers.

onFailure.narration: The water shoves the wall over like a pile of toys. Spray soaks everyone, and the river doesn't even slow down.

walled.narration: But the water piles up behind your wall. It spills over the low ice shelf at the river's edge and swallows Hummock's oldest marker, wavy line and all. Already, a thin stream is sneaking around the end of the wall, back down the old valley. "Well," says Hummock. "Now only the fish can read it."

wall_burst.narration: Your rocks tumble away down the old valley. Hummock wrings out his eyebrows. "Rivers," he says, "are not very good at being told." Pip looks at the water for a long time, and writes something small in his notebook.

follow_water.narration: You sit on the cliff edge and watch. The water fills the old pools one by one, in an order it seems to know by heart. "Remember it," says Hummock. "Somebody will want to know." Watch the order, then tell him.

interaction.cue: Watch the pools fill, then tap them in order.

onSuccess.narration: "Round, long, long, falls," you tell Hummock. He writes it on his sleeve.

onFailure.narration: You mix up two pools. Hummock waits while you watch it all again, and the sun slides lower.

onAssisted.narration: Pip points at each pool as it fills, and you say them together. Hummock writes it on his sleeve.

understood.narration: The water knows its way. It fills every old pool and takes every old bend, like feet finding old slippers in the dark. "I've never seen it," Hummock rumbles, "but my marker has. That wavy line was right all along."

crossing.narration: Back at the fork, the new river runs between you and Hummock's warning post. Low down, a shelf of old ice runs along the water's edge, flat but creaky. High up, wet rocks with Hummock's rope strung between them, slow but solid. "Pick one," says Hummock. "I'll come last. I have to jump."

choices.label: Climb the high rocks on the rope

crossing_flooded.narration: Back at the fork, the new river runs between you and Hummock's warning post. Your wall's water covers the low ice shelf now, knee deep and very cold. High up, wet rocks with Hummock's rope strung between them, slow but solid. "Pick one," says Hummock. "I'll come last. I have to jump."

choices.label: Climb the high rocks on the rope

check_wade.narration: The water is cold enough to make your teeth sing. Under it, the ice is slick. Hummock holds his breath on the bank, which is a lot of breath.
check_wade.prompt: Wade across the flooded shelf, leaning into the current

onSuccess.narration: Step, slide, step. You come out on the far bank, teeth chattering, very proud.

onFailure.narration: The current knocks your feet away. You grab Hummock's rope and haul yourself up onto the high rocks, dripping.

check_ice.narration: The ice groans with every step. Hummock holds his breath on the bank, which is a lot of breath.
check_ice.prompt: Tiptoe across the creaking ice before it cracks

onSuccess.narration: Creak, creak, safe. You step onto the far bank.

onFailure.narration: Crack! The shelf splits under you. You scramble up onto the high rocks and finish that way, wet to the knees.

check_high.narration: The rocks are slick with spray. The rope hums in the wind. "Hand over hand," calls Hummock.
check_high.prompt: Pull yourself along the rope over the slippery rocks

onSuccess.narration: Hand over hand, rock to rock. The far bank, at last.

onFailure.narration: Your hands slip, and you slide down the rocks onto the low ice. It creaks, but it holds, and you shuffle the rest of the way, shaking.

hold_ice.narration: Your thornguard steps out onto the ice and braces, shield down, feet wide. The cracks stop spreading. "Steady on," says Hummock, impressed. One by one, everyone crosses behind the thornguard, and the ice holds like a held breath.

across_low.narration: You came over by the low ice shelf. Pip counts everyone's toes, twice, to be sure. "All there!"

variants.text: The low ice is under water now, so you splash across it, knee deep and gasping.

across_high.narration: You came over by the high rocks. Pip's paws are scraped, and he is very proud of them. "Explorer paws," he says.

far_bank.narration: On the far bank, you turn around. Hummock is still on the other side, holding his lantern high. "Too heavy for that ice, too big for those rocks," he calls. "There's a narrow spot I can jump. But the water surges every few breaths. Call me when it drops!"

hummock_jump.narration: The water surges, then drops, then surges. Hummock crouches at the narrow spot, lantern held high. Call out the moment the water drops.

onSuccess.narration: "NOW!" Hummock leaps and lands with a thump that shakes snow off the trees. He doesn't spill a drop of lantern oil.

onFailure.narration: You call a breath too soon. Hummock lands in the surge, up to his middle. He wades out, but his lantern is gone, bobbing away down the old valley.

onAssisted.narration: Pip waves both paws when the water drops, and you all shout together. Hummock leaps and lands with a thump.

lantern_post.narration: Hummock's warning post leans by the old path. The sun is getting low. Somewhere up the valley, the evening sled is on its way. How will you warn it?

choices.label: Light Hummock's lantern on the post
Build a big stone arrow on the path
Run up the path and stop the sled

variants.text: Far up the valley, bells jingle already. "No time to build," says Hummock.
Hummock pats the empty hook on his post. "No lantern," he sighs.

light_lantern.narration: The wind keeps puffing at the wick. "Strike when it dips," says Hummock, shielding it with both enormous hands.

interaction.cue: Strike the flint when the wind dips.

onSuccess.narration: The lantern flares and swings bright on its post.

onFailure.narration: The wind blows out every spark. And there go the bells, coming closer! "Run!" says Hummock.

onAssisted.narration: Pip cups his paws around the wick too. The lantern flares and swings bright on its post.

stone_arrow.narration: Lay flat stones in a giant arrow pointing away from the water. "Big as a sled," says Hummock. "Tail by the water, point up the safe path."

interaction.cue: Lay the arrow so it points away from the water.

options.label: Point stones, up the safe path

clues: Start at the water's edge with the tail.
The long shaft runs from the tail up the slope.
Finish with the point, aimed up the safe path.

onSuccess.narration: A big stone arrow points up the safe path.

onFailure.narration: A stone slips, and the arrow comes out as a squiggle. Nobody would follow that. Bells! "Run!" says Hummock.

onAssisted.narration: Hummock carries the biggest stones, and the arrow is done in no time.

warning_lit.narration: Jingle, jingle. A sled comes around the bend, sees your warning and swishes to a stop. "Well, I never," says a voice.

check_sledge.narration: Bells jingle around the bend. A sled, a big one, coming fast. "Wave!" cries Pip.
check_sledge.prompt: Run up the path, waving, before the sled reaches the water

onSuccess.narration: You wave so hard your arms nearly come off. The sled swishes to a stop, just in time.

onFailure.narration: The sled can't stop in time, so it swerves, straight into a snowbank, and you with it. Everyone is fine. Everyone is snowy.

sledge_stops.narration: Out of the sled climbs a yeti grandmother in a scarf three times her length. "Grandma Drift," she says, "with soup for the reading room. What is that river doing in my valley?" Hummock tells her. She stares at the water. "My grandmother told a story about a river that got lost," she says. "I thought it was just a story."

driver.narration: "This soup has to reach the reading room tonight," says Grandma Drift. "Hot." The safe way is the high path: steep, and her sled is heavy. Or the edge of the old valley, firm in some places and mud in others, and the light is going. How will you get her around?

choices.label: Haul her sled up the high path

check_haul.narration: Everyone grabs a rope. Grandma Drift pushes from behind and gives orders from in front, somehow.
check_haul.prompt: Haul the heavy sled up the steep high path

onSuccess.narration: Up and over she goes, soup and all.

onFailure.narration: The sled tips on the last bump. Half the soup slops out, mostly onto Hummock. He licks his elbow. "Not bad."

check_guide.narration: Some stones are firm. Some are mud pretending to be stones. "Choose well," says Grandma Drift.
check_guide.prompt: Pick out the firm ground, step by step, in the fading light

onSuccess.narration: You find the firm ground step by step, and she glides along behind you.

onFailure.narration: One runner slides into the mud. You heave it out, but half the soup slops away. Some fish are having a very good evening.

dusk.narration: As the sun touches the ridge, the river shivers. Then, all at once, it turns. Water rushes back past the fork, into its own valley, so fast it splashes up the bank and snatches Pip's notebook right off a rock! "My notes!"
dusk.prompt: Grab Pip's notebook before the water carries it off

onSuccess.narration: You snatch it out of the foam, dripping but whole.

onFailure.narration: It whirls away. You chase it along the bank and catch it at last, but the pages have run like soup.

river_back.narration: Then it's quiet. The river runs in its own valley again, as if nothing happened. The old valley lies empty and shining, its pools full, its waterfall dripping. Pip sits down. "It went to its old home," he says. "Then it came back to this one. Which home is home?"

variants.text: "It didn't need our wall," says Hummock gently. "It came back by itself."
Hummock looks down the old valley, where his lantern went. "I'll hang a new one tomorrow."

rest.narration: Hummock's hut is small for a yeti and huge for everyone else. Grandma Drift has gone on up to the reading room, but she left a pot of soup on his stove. Hummock's eyebrows drip as they thaw. "Sleep by the stove," he says, "or go and see the old valley by moonlight. It won't look like that again for a long time."

choices.label: Watch the old valley by moonlight

variants.text: With half her soup spilled, she could only leave a little. Everyone gets a careful half cup. Hummock's elbow is not offered.

check_moon.narration: Moonlight on wet stones. Pools, puddles, a sleepy owl. "Look for the pattern," says Hummock.
check_moon.prompt: Pick out the pattern the old pools make in the moonlight

onSuccess.narration: In the moonlight, the old pools shine in one long line, pointing north, back toward the glacier. Pip draws it fast.

onFailure.narration: Clouds slide over the moon. You see wet stones and one owl, who sees you back. You trudge in, cold to the toes.

account.narration: In the morning, Pip opens his notebook. "What do I write for Lady Olivia?" "Write it for the reading room first," says Hummock. "The yetis' memory ice is kept by an old yeti called Elder Murmur. The ice remembers rivers. Show her the river you crossed, and ask her: has it ever run there before?"

variants.text: Pip writes that you crossed by the high rocks, scraped paws and all.
Pip writes that you crossed by the low ice shelf.
He copies the order the old pools filled: round, long, long, falls.
He writes about the wall too, and how the river came back without it.
He adds the moonlit pools, all pointing north.
His wet pages have run, so he draws both rivers again from memory, the best he can.

ending.narration: So here is your piece. For one day, the river went back down a valley it ran long ago, filled its old pools and woke its old falls, and then came home again. Your Listening Chime still leans north, toward the glacier, and hums a little louder than before. "Up to the reading room?" says Pip. Behind you, the road runs back to the counting stones. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Hummock's oldest marker is still under your wall's water. You'll have to tell the elder about the wavy line from memory.
